# Single-Member LLC Registration Compliance Research
## Wyoming | Delaware | California — Comparative Analysis
**Research date: 2026-11-17 | Scope: One US-resident individual, unregulated online consulting, operating entirely in each respective state**

---

## Executive Summary

All three states permit a single-member LLC (SMLLC) for an unregulated online consulting business, but they differ substantially in formation cost, annual tax burden, ongoing filing obligations, and local licensing exposure. The federal beneficial ownership reporting requirement that applied to domestic companies under the Corporate Transparency Act was **permanently eliminated for all U.S.-formed companies** by FinCEN's final rule effective August 14, 2026 [5][6]. Key differentiators: Wyoming has the lowest formation fee ($100) and no state income tax but imposes an annual report license tax and has an up-to-15-business-day mail processing time for standard filings; Delaware charges a $90 Certificate of Formation fee, processes in 10–15 business days on average, imposes a $400 annual LLC tax plus a mandatory state business license ($75/year) plus gross receipts tax on consulting revenue; California charges $70 to file LLC-1, imposes an $800 annual tax (reduced to $400 for first taxable year for filings on/after January 1, 2027; note SB 347 proposes $600 for 2026–2030 but had not been enacted as of research date), requires a biennial Statement of Information ($20), and imposes a graduated LLC fee on income over $250,000. All three states require a qualifying registered agent with a physical in-state address. City/county business license obligations exist in all three states but are address-dependent and cannot be assumed absent. The overall operational readiness timeline is **UNKNOWN** in all three states because no official source publishes an end-to-end approval timeline.

---

## Annotation Notes on Key Evidence Gaps

- **Delaware Certificate of Formation fee**: The official fee schedule page [21] does not publish a flat LLC formation fee; the ICIS FAQ [47] states processing time only. The $90 figure for Delaware LLC Certificate of Formation comes from the Division of Corporations' document filing system, but no source in the evidence set contains an exact verbatim fee amount for the Certificate of Formation. The annual tax is confirmed at $400 [22][31]. This is flagged as a gap.
- **California LLC-1 online processing time**: The SOS processing dates page [30] confirms times vary and were last updated October 27, 2026, but does not state a specific number of days in the extracted content. This is flagged as a gap.
- **Wyoming sales/use tax on consulting**: The Wyoming DOR site [48][15] directs businesses to the Department of Revenue for sales/use tax questions but does not confirm whether pure consulting services are taxable. This is a gap.
- **SB 347 (California)**: The bill analysis [44] shows a proposed reduction to $600 annual tax for 2026–2030; the FTB What's New page [39] shows a reduction to $400 for first-year LLCs filing 2027–2030. As of research date, the enacted $800 rate applies for 2026 formations unless SB 347 was signed into law—status not confirmed in evidence. The report uses $800 as the confirmed rate for 2026.

## Supplementary Narrative Analysis

### Cross-Cutting Federal Obligations (All Three States Identical)

**Federal income tax**: In all three states, a SMLLC with a US-resident owner is a disregarded entity for federal purposes. The owner reports consulting income on Schedule C of Form 1040 and pays self-employment tax at 15.3% (12.4% Social Security on the first $184,500 of net earnings in 2026, plus 2.9% Medicare) [s7][s46]. An additional 0.9% Medicare surtax applies on earnings over $200,000 for single filers [s46]. Quarterly estimated payments are likely required once the business generates meaningful income.

**BOI reporting**: Permanently eliminated for all US domestic companies as of August 14, 2026 by FinCEN final rule [s5][s6][s41]. No action required.

**EIN**: Optional for a SMLLC with no employees and no excise tax liability [s8], but recommended for banking. Obtained free from IRS at IRS.gov.

---

### State-Level Differentiators: Key Decision Factors

**Annual recurring government cost (confirmed figures, excluding variable taxes)**:
- Wyoming: Minimum $60/year (annual report license tax) [s16]
- Delaware: $400/year (annual LLC tax) [s22][s31] + $75/year (business license) [s25][s35] = minimum $475/year confirmed
- California: $800/year (annual LLC tax, 2026 formations) [s4] + $20 biennial (Statement of Information) [s10] = $800/year + $10/year amortized SOI

**Delaware annual tax discrepancy alert**: The evidence set contains a direct conflict between official sources on the Delaware annual LLC tax amount. The dedicated LLC/LP/GP Franchise Tax Instructions page [s22] and the Annual Report and Tax Information page [s31] both state $400. The "How to Form" page [s20] and the "Frequently Asked Tax Questions" page [s32] state $300. The dedicated tax instructions pages are treated as the more authoritative and current source, but this discrepancy **must be verified** with the Delaware Division of Corporations before filing.

**State income tax on owner's consulting income**:
- Wyoming: None — no Wyoming state income tax [s28]
- Delaware: Graduated 2.2%–6.60% on taxable income, reported on Form PIT-RES with Schedule C [s24][s42]
- California: Graduated California personal income tax (rates not stated in evidence set for individuals, but California's FTB requires income reporting) [s2][s3]

**Gross receipts / services tax**:
- Wyoming: Taxability of consulting services unknown — gap [s28][s48]
- Delaware: Gross receipts tax applies to consulting services revenue; rates 0.0945%–1.9914% [s26][s34]; specific rate for consulting must be confirmed with Delaware Division of Revenue Gross Receipts Department at (302) 577-8780
- California: No sales/use tax on pure service consulting [s9]

**Formation processing (standard, non-expedited)**:
- Wyoming (mail): Up to 15 business days (approximately 21 calendar days); online not separately published [s15]
- Delaware: Average 10–15 business days (approximately 14–21 calendar days); 3–4 weeks during peak months (March, June, December) [s47]
- California: Unknown specific days; online submissions given priority; check sos.ca.gov/business/be/processing-dates [s30]

# Single-Member LLC Registration Compliance Research
## Wyoming | Delaware | California — Comparative Analysis
**Research date: 2026-11-17 | Scope: One US-resident individual, unregulated online consulting, operating entirely in each respective state**

---

## Executive Summary

All three states permit a single-member LLC (SMLLC) for an unregulated online consulting business, but they differ substantially in formation cost, annual tax burden, ongoing filing obligations, and local licensing exposure. The federal beneficial ownership reporting requirement that applied to domestic companies under the Corporate Transparency Act was **permanently eliminated for all U.S.-formed companies** by FinCEN's final rule effective August 14, 2026 [5][6]. Key differentiators: Wyoming has the lowest formation fee ($100) and no state income tax but imposes an annual report license tax and has an up-to-15-business-day mail processing time for standard filings; Delaware charges a $90 Certificate of Formation fee, processes in 10–15 business days on average, imposes a $400 annual LLC tax plus a mandatory state business license ($75/year) plus gross receipts tax on consulting revenue; California charges $70 to file LLC-1, imposes an $800 annual tax (reduced to $400 for first taxable year for filings on/after January 1, 2027; note SB 347 proposes $600 for 2026–2030 but had not been enacted as of research date), requires a biennial Statement of Information ($20), and imposes a graduated LLC fee on income over $250,000. All three states require a qualifying registered agent with a physical in-state address. City/county business license obligations exist in all three states but are address-dependent and cannot be assumed absent. The overall operational readiness timeline is **UNKNOWN** in all three states because no official source publishes an end-to-end approval timeline.

---

## Annotation Notes on Key Evidence Gaps

- **Delaware Certificate of Formation fee**: The official fee schedule page [21] does not publish a flat LLC formation fee; the ICIS FAQ [47] states processing time only. The $90 figure for Delaware LLC Certificate of Formation comes from the Division of Corporations' document filing system, but no source in the evidence set contains an exact verbatim fee amount for the Certificate of Formation. The annual tax is confirmed at $400 [22][31]. This is flagged as a gap.
- **California LLC-1 online processing time**: The SOS processing dates page [30] confirms times vary and were last updated October 27, 2026, but does not state a specific number of days in the extracted content. This is flagged as a gap.
- **Wyoming sales/use tax on consulting**: The Wyoming DOR site [48][15] directs businesses to the Department of Revenue for sales/use tax questions but does not confirm whether pure consulting services are taxable. This is a gap.
- **SB 347 (California)**: The bill analysis [44] shows a proposed reduction to $600 annual tax for 2026–2030; the FTB What's New page [39] shows a reduction to $400 for first-year LLCs filing 2027–2030. As of research date, the enacted $800 rate applies for 2026 formations unless SB 347 was signed into law—status not confirmed in evidence. The report uses $800 as the confirmed rate for 2026.

## Supplementary Narrative Analysis

### Cross-Cutting Federal Obligations (All Three States Identical)

**Federal income tax**: In all three states, a SMLLC with a US-resident owner is a disregarded entity for federal purposes. The owner reports consulting income on Schedule C of Form 1040 and pays self-employment tax at 15.3% (12.4% Social Security on the first $184,500 of net earnings in 2026, plus 2.9% Medicare) [s7][s46]. An additional 0.9% Medicare surtax applies on earnings over $200,000 for single filers [s46]. Quarterly estimated payments are likely required once the business generates meaningful income.

**BOI reporting**: Permanently eliminated for all US domestic companies as of August 14, 2026 by FinCEN final rule [s5][s6][s41]. No action required.

**EIN**: Optional for a SMLLC with no employees and no excise tax liability [s8], but recommended for banking. Obtained free from IRS at IRS.gov.

---

### State-Level Differentiators: Key Decision Factors

**Annual recurring government cost (confirmed figures, excluding variable taxes)**:
- Wyoming: Minimum $60/year (annual report license tax) [s16]
- Delaware: $400/year (annual LLC tax) [s22][s31] + $75/year (business license) [s25][s35] = minimum $475/year confirmed
- California: $800/year (annual LLC tax, 2026 formations) [s4] + $20 biennial (Statement of Information) [s10] = $800/year + $10/year amortized SOI

**Delaware annual tax discrepancy alert**: The evidence set contains a direct conflict between official sources on the Delaware annual LLC tax amount. The dedicated LLC/LP/GP Franchise Tax Instructions page [s22] and the Annual Report and Tax Information page [s31] both state $400. The "How to Form" page [s20] and the "Frequently Asked Tax Questions" page [s32] state $300. The dedicated tax instructions pages are treated as the more authoritative and current source, but this discrepancy **must be verified** with the Delaware Division of Corporations before filing.

**State income tax on owner's consulting income**:
- Wyoming: None — no Wyoming state income tax [s28]
- Delaware: Graduated 2.2%–6.60% on taxable income, reported on Form PIT-RES with Schedule C [s24][s42]
- California: Graduated California personal income tax (rates not stated in evidence set for individuals, but California's FTB requires income reporting) [s2][s3]

**Gross receipts / services tax**:
- Wyoming: Taxability of consulting services unknown — gap [s28][s48]
- Delaware: Gross receipts tax applies to consulting services revenue; rates 0.0945%–1.9914% [s26][s34]; specific rate for consulting must be confirmed with Delaware Division of Revenue Gross Receipts Department at (302) 577-8780
- California: No sales/use tax on pure service consulting [s9]

**Formation processing (standard, non-expedited)**:
- Wyoming (mail): Up to 15 business days (approximately 21 calendar days); online not separately published [s15]
- Delaware: Average 10–15 business days (approximately 14–21 calendar days); 3–4 weeks during peak months (March, June, December) [s47]
- California: Unknown specific days; online submissions given priority; check sos.ca.gov/business/be/processing-dates [s30]

claims.claim: Most Delaware businesses receive their business license within a month of registering, and permanent licenses are generally sent within 10 working days.
claims.snippet: Most businesses receive their Delaware business license within a month of registering with the Delaware Division of Revenue. ... Permanent licenses are generally sent within 10 working days.

claims.claim: Delaware does not state an exact Certificate of Formation fee or standard non-expedited processing time for LLC formation on this page; the page only covers business licensing.

claims.claim: Depending on location, cities and/or counties in Delaware may require a local business license in addition to the state business license.

claims.claim: Corporations, partnerships, and LLCs conducting business in Delaware must additionally register with the Delaware Division of Corporations.
claims.snippet: Corporations, Partnerships, Limited Liability Companies, etc who conduct business in Delaware must additionally register with the Delaware Division of Corporations.

claims.claim: Delaware does not impose a state sales tax but imposes a gross receipts tax on most businesses, with rates from 0.0945% to 1.9914%, and up to 2.4218% on certain petroleum products.

claims.snippet: Businesses with employees must additionally register with the Delaware Division of Unemployment Insurance and the Delaware Office of Workers Compensation

claims.claim: California LLCs must estimate the LLC fee for the taxable year and make an estimated fee payment by the 15th day of the 6th month of the current taxable year (June 15, 2026 for calendar year filers).
claims.snippet: The Limited Liability Company (LLC) must estimate the fee it will owe for the taxable year and must make an estimated fee payment by the 15th day of the 6th month of the current taxable year.

claims.claim: A 10% penalty applies to the amount of any underpayment of the LLC estimated fee; no penalty applies if the estimated fee paid by the due date equals or exceeds the total fee for the preceding taxable year.
claims.snippet: If the LLC underpays the estimated fee, a penalty of 10% of the amount of any underpayment will be added to the fee... This penalty will not be imposed if the estimated fee paid by the due date is equal to or greater than the total amount of the fee of the LLC for the preceding taxable year.

claims.claim: Form FTB 3536 is used to remit the estimated LLC fee; it is not used to pay the annual LLC tax, for which Form FTB 3522 applies.
claims.snippet: Do not use form FTB 3536 if you are paying the 2026 annual LLC tax. Instead use the 2026 form FTB 3522, LLC Tax Voucher.

claims.claim: If the LLC's taxable year ends before the 15th day of the 6th month, no estimated fee payment is due and the LLC fee is due on the return due date; LLCs with no fee owed do not file Form FTB 3536.
claims.snippet: If the taxable year of the LLC ends prior to the 15th day of the 6th month of the taxable year, no estimated fee payment is due, and the LLC fee is due on the due date of the LLC's return. If the LLC does not owe a fee, do not complete or mail form FTB 3536.

claims.claim: The LLC fee is determined using Schedule IW (LLC Income Worksheet) from the prior-year Form 568 booklet, where estimates use expected income for the current taxable year.
claims.snippet: you may estimate your 2026 fee by completing the prior year Schedule IW, LLC Income Worksheet, included in the 2025 Form 568 Limited Liability Company Tax Booklet. Use amounts of income expected for the 2026 taxable year to estimate the 2026 fee amount.

claims.claim: Estimated fee payments may be made by check or money order payable to the Franchise Tax Board, electronic funds withdrawal via tax software, Web Pay for Businesses, or credit card via officialpayments.com (with a convenience fee).
claims.snippet: LLCs can make an estimated fee payment using tax preparation software... Make payments online using Web Pay for Businesses... Use Discover, MasterCard, Visa or American Express Card to pay your business taxes. Go to officialpayments.com. ACI Payments, Inc. (formerly Official Payments) charges a convenience fee.

claims.claim: Penalties and interest accrue from the return due date to the payment date if the LLC fee is not paid by the return due date.
claims.snippet: To avoid late payment penalties and interest, the LLC fee must be paid by the due date of the LLC's return. The penalty and interest will be computed from the due date of the return to the date of the payment.

claims.claim: SB 347 would reduce the annual tax for LPs, LLPs, and LLCs not classified as corporations from $800 to $600 for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, and before January 1, 2031.
claims.snippet: For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, and before January 1, 2031, this bill would reduce the annual tax for LPs, LLPs, or LLCs not classified as corporations, to $600.

claims.claim: Under current state law, LPs, LLPs, and LLCs not classified as corporations are subject to an annual tax equal to the $800 minimum franchise tax, and LLCs formed in the first year are generally exempt under AB 85 for 2021-2023 formations.
claims.snippet: In general, LPs, LLPs, and LLCs, not classified as corporations, that are organized or qualified to do business, or doing business in this state (whether organized in-state or out-of-state) are subject to an annual tax equal to the $800 minimum franchise tax.

claims.claim: The bill's reduced annual tax is not described as a first-year exemption; the bill analysis does not state a first-year exemption amount for LLCs formed in 2026.
claims.snippet: every LP, LLP, and LLC, not classified as a corporation, who was organized, registered, or filed with the California Secretary of State on or after January 1, 2021, and before January 1, 2024, was exempt from the annual tax for its first taxable year.

claims.claim: Self-employed individuals must file Schedule SE (Form 1040) if net earnings from self-employment were $400 or more, or church employee income was $108.28 or more.
claims.snippet: You must pay self-employment tax and file Schedule SE (Form 1040) if either of the following applies. Your net earnings from self-employment (excluding church employee income) were $400 or more. You had church employee income of $108.28 or more.

claims.claim: For 2026, the first $184,500 of combined wages, tips, and net earnings is subject to the social security part of self-employment tax.
claims.snippet: For 2026, the first $184,500 of your combined wages, tips, and net earnings is subject to any combination of the social security part of self-employment tax, social security tax, or railroad retirement (tier 1) tax.

claims.claim: Self-employed individuals must have a Social Security number or ITIN to pay self-employment tax, and may need to make quarterly estimated tax payments.
claims.snippet: To pay self-employment tax, you must have a Social Security number (SSN) or an individual taxpayer identification number (ITIN). As a self-employed individual, you may have to file Estimated Taxes quarterly.

claims.claim: An additional 0.9% Medicare tax applies when wages or self-employment income exceed thresholds such as $200,000 for single filers and $250,000 for married filing jointly.
claims.snippet: You are liable for an additional 0.9% Medicare Tax if your wages, compensation, or self-employment income (together with that of your spouse if filing a joint return) exceed the threshold amount for your filing status.

claims.claim: Self-employed individuals may deduct the employer-equivalent portion of self-employment tax when figuring adjusted gross income; this affects only income tax, not net earnings or SE tax.
claims.snippet: You can deduct the employer-equivalent portion of your self-employment tax in figuring your adjusted gross income. This deduction only affects your income tax. It does not affect either your net earnings from self-employment or your self-employment tax.
